newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Police arrest 36 in Mozambique protests.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest 36 in Mozambique protests.

text.p: The Mozambican police arrested at least 36 people on Monday for taking part in demonstrations called by the former rebel movement Renamo, according to media reports from three towns on Tuesday.
The Mozambique News Agency and the Maputo daily Noticias said 15 people had been arrested in the northern town of Nampula and nine in Angoche, a coastal town in the north.
Noticias said a further 12 people were arrested and three injured at a Renamo demonstration in the port city of Beira.
The demonstrations were in protest against the high cost of living and alleged "misgovernment" by the ruling Frelimo Party.
The arrests took place because Renamo did not follow the legal rules for demonstrations in public places, police said.
Under 1991 legislation the organisers of any demonstration in a public place must give written notice to the local authorities and police at least four working days in advance.
Organisers must submit the route and marches may only take place outside of working hours.
Monday's protests were the latest in a wave of Renamo demonstrations. A week ago a demonstration in Beira led to clashes with the riot police in which 25 people were detained.
